candidate.answerReason: An odd sum of two primes must include 2, but the remaining summand would be 45, which is composite.

methods.label: Use the only even prime
methods.explanation:
Because \(47\) is odd, its two summands must consist of one even number and one odd number. The only even prime is \(2\): every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself. Thus any possible pair of primes would have to be \(2\) and
\[
47-2=45.
\]
But \(45=5\times9\), so \(45\) is not prime. This rules out every possible pair, regardless of order. There are \(0\) ways, choice A.
methods.levelReason: Elementary odd-even reasoning and the definition of a prime eliminate all possibilities without a long search.

candidate.annotationRationale: Prime and composite numbers are the central target. Parity restricts the possible prime pair, and factor meaning justifies both the uniqueness of the even prime and the rejection of 45.
